title: sleep2vec: Unified Cross-Modal Alignment for Heterogeneous Nocturnal Biosignals
claim: Real-world monitoring yields many concurrent, heterogeneous signals at different sampling rates that all reflect one shared underlying state.
layout: 2 columns of stacked signal cards flanking a central patient illustration
description: A cartoon-style illustration of a patient lying in bed in the center, wearing a nasal cannula and with cables running to a bedside monitor. Flanking the patient are two columns of rounded cards, each holding a small icon, a label, and a colored waveform. The left column is headed 'High Sampling Rate Channels' and has EEG, EMG, EOG and ECG, with dense noisy traces in teal, brown, mauve and red. The right column is headed 'Low Sampling Rate Channels' and has IBI, Nasal Airflow, ABD/Thor Belt, Respiratory and SpO2, with smoother, slower waveforms in pink, green, tan, gray and blue. Each card has its own color. Cards partly overlap the patient with a faded edge. The eye goes first to the colorful waveform stacks and then to the patient.
caption: Polysomnography (PSG) captures diverse physiological signals, illustrated here as 30-second segments for each modality. High sampling rate electrophysiological channels include EEG, EMG, EOG, and ECG, while lower sampling rate cardiopulmonary and oximetry channels encompass Nasal Airflow, Abdominal/Thoracic Belt (ABD/Thor Belt), and SpO$_2$. Inter-Beat Interval (IBI) and Respiratory effort (RESP) are interval-derived features computed from ECG and respiratory channels (ABD/Thor Belts when available, otherwise Nasal Airflow), respectively. Together, these concurrent nocturnal signals provide complementary perspectives on a shared latent physiological state, highlighting the multimodal complexity inherent to sleep monitoring.
abstract: Tasks ranging from sleep staging to clinical diagnosis traditionally rely on standard polysomnography (PSG) devices, bedside monitors and wearable devices, which capture diverse nocturnal biosignals (e.g., EEG, EOG, ECG, SpO$_2$). However, heterogeneity across devices and frequent sensor dropout pose significant challenges for unified modelling of these multimodal signals. We present \texttt{sleep2vec}, a foundation model for diverse and incomplete nocturnal biosignals that learns a shared representation via cross-modal alignment. \texttt{sleep2vec} is contrastively pre-trained on 42,249 overnight recordings spanning nine modalities using a \textit{Demography, Age, Site \& History-aware InfoNCE} objective that incorporates physiological and acquisition metadata (\textit{e.g.}, age, gender, recording site) to dynamically weight negatives and mitigate cohort-specific shortcuts. On downstream sleep staging and clinical outcome assessment, \texttt{sleep2vec} consistently outperforms strong baselines and remains robust to any subset of available modalities and sensor dropout. We further characterize, to our knowledge for the first time, scaling laws for nocturnal biosignals with respect to modality diversity and model capacity. Together, these results show that unified cross-modal alignment, coupled with principled scaling, enables label-efficient, general-purpose modelling of real-world nocturnal biosignals.
